nodes.label: Pressure is defended by baroreflex tachycardia, not by reduced loss. Heart ra...
nodes.statement: Pressure is defended by baroreflex tachycardia, not by reduced loss. Heart rate rises monotonically with severity (71 -> 110 /min) while cardiac output still falls (5.75 -> 3.95 L/min); MAP is held only while the tachycardia offsets the volume loss and breaks once the bleed outruns it (severity >= 0.6). The compensation is Pulse's own cardiovascular reflex, not an imposed term.

nodes.label: The improvement is produced by the engineered MapFluidController, not by the ...
nodes.statement: The improvement is produced by the engineered MapFluidController, not by the fluid itself. The loop watches MAP and commands infusion only once it falls below the 90 mmHg target, so the intervention is late (t=508 s) and small (79.6 mL); the restored volume, not the compound, drives the +78 mL / +2.2 mmHg gain. This is an engineered control term added to the composite, distinct from Pulse's own reflexes.

nodes.label: The fraction-volume trend follows from a shared compensation, not from differ...
nodes.statement: The fraction-volume trend follows from a shared compensation, not from different responses per patient. Every patient runs Pulse's same baroreflex (F-01), and the absolute loss is much less variable (1094-1755 mL) than the starting volume (2881-7072 mL); because a similar absolute loss is taken from very different reserves, the fraction lost falls as starting volume rises (rho = -0.91). The uniform mechanism, not patient-specific physiology, produces the correlation.
